notes: The provided `dist/mcp-server.js` is minified and several relevant helper implementations are truncated or hidden behind helper calls (`Nt`, `an`, `mn`, `on`, `Jt`), so some output-field details are marked undetermined.

README documentation conflicts with the bundled code about the default tool tier: README says `all` is the default at README.md:296 and README.md:352, but the source code in `nr()` defaults to `core` at dist/mcp-server.js:44, so the source-code behavior is used.

expand_task.rationale: `expand_task` resolves the user's task file with `T({projectRoot:e.projectRoot,file:e.file},t)` and calls `Jt({tasksJsonPath:a,id:e.id,num:e.num,research:e.research,prompt:e.prompt,...})`, returning the helper's result. It reads/writes non-public project task data. The `research` flag is passed through and described as using a research role, so when enabled output may include attacker-controllable web/search content. Exact returned fields are hidden in helper `Jt`, so field detail is undetermined.

get_task.rationale: `get_task` is advertised/registered as `get_task:Nt` and included in the default `$n` core tool set; the changelog describes the MCP `get_task` tool returning structured task objects. This exposes non-public task details from the user's project/account. The implementation body for `Nt` is not visible in the provided truncated bundle, so returned fields are undetermined.

get_tasks.rationale: `get_tasks` reads task data through `n.tasks.list({tag:o,filter:e,includeSubtasks:a})` and returns it as `data:{tasks:c,...}`; task data comes from the user's Task Master project/account and is non-public. It is in the default `$n` core tool set.

next_task.rationale: `next_task` resolves the user's task file and optional complexity report (`de(e,n)`, `fe({...e,tag:r},n)`) and returns the result of `an({tasksJsonPath:a,reportPath:o,projectRoot:e.projectRoot,tag:r},...)`. This exposes non-public local/project task data. Exact returned fields are produced by helper `an`, which is not shown in the provided source, so output field detail is undetermined. It is in the default `$n` core tool set.

parse_prd.rationale: `parse_prd` accepts an `input` PRD file path and `projectRoot`, calls `on({...e,tag:a},...)`, and returns the result. It reads the user's local PRD and writes generated task data, so returned content can expose non-public project requirements. Although it may call configured AI providers, those are fixed vendor endpoints rather than attacker-chosen destinations. The helper body is not shown, so returned fields are undetermined.

set_task_status.rationale: `set_task_status` updates local/account task records via `n.tasks.updateStatus(r,i,o)` and returns `data:{message:...,tasks:s}` including prior/new status data from the user's task store. That returned task status information is non-public project/account data. It is in the default `$n` core tool set.

update_subtask.rationale: `update_subtask` resolves a task file with `T({projectRoot:e.projectRoot,file:e.file},t)`, writes to the selected subtask via `mn({tasksJsonPath:o,id:e.id,prompt:e.prompt,research:e.research,...})`, and returns that helper's result. It can expose non-public local/project task data. The `research` argument is passed through and described as using Perplexity/research-backed updates, so when enabled the returned/stored text may incorporate attacker-controllable web/search content. Exact returned fields are hidden in helper `mn`, so field detail is undetermined.

value_conditions.default: applies when the variable is missing or blank
value_conditions.effect: Defaults to `core`; the core list `$n` enables all seven advertised tools: `get_tasks`, `next_task`, `get_task`, `set_task_status`, `update_subtask`, `parse_prd`, and `expand_task`.

value_conditions.default: not required because unset already defaults to `core`
value_conditions.effect: Loads only `$n`, which includes all seven advertised tools.
Loads `er`, the standard set, which includes all core tools plus additional tools; all seven advertised tools remain enabled.
Loads `Object.keys($)`, enabling every registered tool; all seven advertised tools remain enabled.
Loads only the valid named tools after name normalization; any advertised tool omitted from the list is removed. If no valid names are found, the code falls back to loading all tools.
